component.title: Trust tier badge
component.purpose: Shows which of the four ordered trust tiers a contact holds, as a rank rather than a category, so two tiers can be compared at a glance the way the room ceiling compares them.

states.description: A known contact, the ordinary case.
A stranger, the default for any unrecognised sender.
A long handle that must not break the badge's shape.

claims.statement: The four tiers read as an ordered ladder, so a lower tier is recognisable as lower without reading the label.
claims.rationale: The room ceiling is a minimum across tiers; if tiers do not look ordered, the ceiling rule cannot be understood.

claims.statement: Tiers are distinguishable without relying on colour alone.
The stranger tier is presented as the ordinary default rather than as an error condition.
claims.rationale: Every unrecognised sender is a stranger by design. Styling it as a fault would make the normal case look broken.

claims.statement: The badge announces the tier name, not only a colour or a glyph.

priorities.statement: How that tier compares to the others
